decisions.reason: As a recently launched security offering that is already publicly presented on the website, management is likely to continue backing it and interpret any early market frictions as temporary.

This digital-signature function fits closely with a German software firm's existing capabilities, so after investing in launch and promotion management would be inclined to retain it rather than reverse course quickly.

A multi-layer end-to-end security architecture appears central to the firm's strategic positioning in secure communications, making withdrawal soon after launch unlikely despite any initial uncertainty.
Although this looks more niche than the core security architecture products, the firm has still made a visible market commitment and would likely give it more time before admitting a weak start.

Because a hardware signature token is somewhat less natural for a medium-sized software and consultancy firm, it has the highest withdrawal risk, but escalation of commitment still makes near-term continuation more likely than an immediate exit.

A payment-network security compliance suite matches both enterprise demand and the firm's advisory profile, so management would likely persist with it after the initial launch investment and public commitment.
